def transform(grid):
    # Fill the interior of each rectangular monochrome outline with the
    # digit determined by the frame dimensions (deduced from demonstrations).
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    seen = set()
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            color = grid[r][c]
            if color in (6, 9) or (r, c) in seen:
                continue
            # connected component of same-colored cells
            stack = [(r, c)]; seen.add((r, c)); cells=[]
            while stack:
                y, x = stack.pop(); cells.append((y, x))
                for dy, dx in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)):
                    ny,nx=y+dy,x+dx
                    if 0<=ny<h and 0<=nx<w and (ny,nx) not in seen and grid[ny][nx]==color:
                        seen.add((ny,nx)); stack.append((ny,nx))
            r0=min(y for y,x in cells); r1=max(y for y,x in cells)
            c0=min(x for y,x in cells); c1=max(x for y,x in cells)
            # For a complete one-cell rectangular frame, fill the cavity.
            if len(cells) == 2*(r1-r0+1)+2*(c1-c0+1)-4 and r1-r0>=2 and c1-c0>=2:
                # Demo: 3x3 frames -> 7, 6x6 frame -> 2.
                fill = 7 if (r1-r0+1, c1-c0+1) == (3,3) else 2
                for y in range(r0+1,r1):
                    for x in range(c0+1,c1):
                        out[y][x]=fill
    return out
